text:
maya: Heads-up — p99 latency for hosted/generation has increased ~2.2x in the canary cohort after the runtime/3.4.1 canary rollout (~10:15 UTC). Not steady, shows spikes every 30–90s.
sre-bot: Alert: p99_gen_latency > 1200ms (was ~520ms) — canary pool r3-*-canary.
tony: thanks, @maya. Is this only canary or observed on a few user tenants?
maya: only canary so far, but a handful of internal smoke jobs hit tails. No customer pages yet.
li: I'm digging in metrics now — flamegraphs look like queuing on the "late-binding queue map" path. CPU wait + RT wait spikes on inference workers.
li: quick repro command I used (can run from devbox):
```
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.dev/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/open-7b","input":"token heavy prompt...","max_tokens":256}'
```
maya: thanks, can you paste the logs when you repro? also correlate with canary kernel/tag.
li: repro logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-17T10:18:22Z] recv req id=abcd1234 size=12 routing=hotpath
[2026-02-17T10:18:22Z] batch_wait start=12ms worker=rv-22
[2026-02-17T10:18:22Z] late_bind_map_lock wait=48ms
[2026-02-17T10:18:22Z] inference start=112ms kv_cache:miss
[2026-02-17T10:18:22Z] response send=1300ms
```
ev if it's the late-bind lock, maybe the new scheduler version changed lock granularity. Which patch landed in 3.4.1?
maya: 3.4.1 included: scheduler: late-binding lock refactor, batch-coalescer tweak, kernel selector minor.
carla: can we toggle batch-coalescer config in canary to see impact? If batching waits longer we could get lower throughput but shorter p99s.
ev an alternative: route canary traffic to older scheduler via variant pin and keep rest of runtime changes. That would isolate late-bind refactor.
li: I ran a quick experiment: bumped coalescer.window_ms from 8->4 on one canary shard, p99 dropped ~18% but p95 unchanged. Suggests queuing window matters but not root cause.
tony: we should do a quick bisect across the subpatches in 3.4.1 to find the commit that regressed the late-bind path. @oncall can you allocate a run?
carla: @evan can you prepare a traffic-split to divert 50% of canary to the pre-3.4 scheduler variant? We can observe if p99 returns to baseline.
ev an: setting up split now. Doing canary traffic split: `rb split apply --from canary --to canary-old-sched --ratio 50`
sre-bot: Deploy event: split applied — canary-old-sched receiving 50% traffic (shards r3-{2,5}).
li: early numbers after split: p99 on canary-old-sched ~560ms, p99 on canary-new-sched ~1180ms. So it's almost certainly the late-bind refactor.
maya: ok plan: 1) pause further canary expansion 2) rollback the late-bind refactor in the canary binary (or pin scheduler variant) 3) run targeted bisect on the refactor commits 4) notify support to prepare customer comms if needed.
carla: I'll open the rollback PR to pin scheduler to prev impl for canary.
ev an: rolling pin now, ETA ~7m for new canary shards to take effect.
li: for bisect steps I'll run `git bisect` across the four refactor commits and run the small load repro (100 qps) — will update with commit hash when found.
tony: assign owner for postmortem/notes? @maya you?
maya: I'll take postmortem. @support-bot can you draft an internal support note template we can use if customers ask?
support-bot: Draft: "We observed increased tail latency in canary after a routine runtime update. We have mitigations in place (pinning scheduler variant). If you're seeing production impact, please reply with your organization id and example request IDs. We'll prioritize any customer-facing rollbacks." :white_check_mark:
li: bisect update: found failing commit `commit 7a9f3b2` (scheduler/late_bind: changed lock scope). Reverting that commit on canary brings p99 back to baseline in our repro.
maya: good find. Next steps: merge rollback to canary, hold on wider rollout until we have test coverage + perf regression tests for late-bind lock.
carla: also adding an automated check: synthetic canary that runs 200 qps open-loop on a few payload shapes to catch this class of latencies.
ev an: mitigation completed — canary p99 back to ~540ms. Rolling forward with rollback patch paused for wider rollout.
maya: support/customer action: if we see any customer escalations, routing to support channel #support-ops and include req ids.
support-bot: Noted. I created a ticket template: "Escalation: p99 regression traced to runtime scheduler change; mitigated by scheduler pin on canary; awaiting rollback PR; contact: maya@redwood.com"
tony: thanks everyone. Great bisect and quick pin. We'll follow up with PM/QA to add perf tests before the next scheduler refactor. :thumbsup:
